tldr: The Oregon Prosperity Council, established by Governor Kotek in January 2026, proposes 10 priority recommendations to advance Oregon's long-term economic competitiveness and prosperity. After extensive statewide engagement (66 listening sessions, 1,000+ survey responses), the Council identifies critical challenges: 41% of residents below the ALICE threshold, 49th-worst employment growth, and 5.2% unemployment above the national rate. Priority recommendations span tax reform, permitting acceleration, regulatory relief, site readiness infrastructure ($250M/biennium), and talent alignment, requiring urgent coordinated action to modernize systems and ensure broad-based prosperity.

bullets.text: Governor Kotek established Prosperity Council in January 2026 to advise on Prosperity Roadmap strategies; conducted 66 listening sessions, engaged 25 communities, received 45 letters, and collected 1,000+ survey responses
Oregon ranks 49th in non-farm employment growth and has 5.2% unemployment rate, above national average of 4.3%
41% of Oregonians living below ALICE threshold—either in poverty or unable to afford basic expenditures in their communities
Transform Business Oregon into Oregon Commerce Authority governed by board of business and innovation leaders
Establish $250 million per biennium dedicated site readiness and infrastructure fund using bonding authority
Reduce regulatory and administrative burdens by 20% by 2029 through removal of outdated and duplicative regulations
Establish enforceable statewide permitting timelines requiring agencies to approve or deny complete applications within statutory deadlines
Adopt market-based Cap and Invest program for greenhouse gas emissions; repeal Climate Protection Program upon implementation
